transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-03
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Leo Park (Redwood SE), Priya Desai (CTO, Orion), Marcus Lee (Lead ML Engineer), Sara Gomez (Head of Ops)

Summary: quick intake to understand cost levers and decide pilot path (hosted -> dedicated or private).

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm Maya from Redwood, with Leo our SE. how are you all?
[00:08] Priya Desai: good, thanks. busy week but excited to chat.
[00:12] Marcus Lee: yeah thanks, we've been looking into cost numbers and wanted to run through tradeoffs.
[00:20] Leo Park: great. we put together a short agenda: traffic/profile, desired latency & quality, budget constraints, pilot options (hosted -> dedicated -> private), and next steps. sound right?
[00:31] Priya Desai: yup, that's it. Marcus i'll let you sketch the technical flow.
[00:36] Marcus Lee: sure. so we have a recommendation service that takes user context + browsing history, average prompt length 220 tokens, response ~80 tokens. current qps for recommendations is 40 p95 during peaks, avg 8k requests per minute off peak, expecting growth to 200 p95 in 6 months as we roll out personalization.
[00:56] Sara Gomez: our constraint is budget — we have a quarterly cap we can't exceed and procurement wants predictable spend.
[01:05] Maya Chen: ok that's helpful. two quick clarifying q's: where is your data residency requirement — any region mandates? and do you want managed keys or customer-managed KMS?
[01:15] Priya Desai: US only today, maybe EU next year. we prefer customer-managed keys for production.
[01:21] Leo Park: noted. on the cost levers: per-token unit price is the baseline (hosted API), batching helps amortize fixed overheads, and prefix/KV caching reduces repeated compute when many requests share context. quantization & model variants also change throughput/cost.
[01:36] Marcus Lee: can you quantify that? like what savings are realistic for our profile?
[01:40] Leo Park: rough ballpark — with continuous batching at your QPS, you might see 10-25% savings vs naive per-request inference. if you can cache prefixes (say same user session or same product context) and hit rates of 40-60% on cache keys, that can cut compute work by 30-60% on those requests. together, with a lighter quantized model in Dedicated, customers often see 2-4x reduction in per-unit cost vs initial hosted rate. but i want to emphasize those depend heavily on prompt distribution and session locality.
[02:10] Priya Desai: 2-4x is big. what's the tradeoff in latency and quality? we can't compromise 95th percentile latency beyond 120ms.
[02:20] Leo Park: Hosted is optimized for fast time-to-value, 95th percentiles vary by model but we'd expect low single-digit 100s ms for our smaller models. Dedicated gives more predictable tail latency because you control capacity and there's less noisy neighbor interference. Private (VPC/on-prem) is similar to Dedicated in latency but you take on infra ops. quantization can add a small accuracy delta; we test with your eval prompts to quantify impact — sometimes negligible for ranking tasks.
[02:46] Marcus Lee: can we do a benchmark where we test the quantized candidate model and measure hit rate and latency?
[02:50] Leo Park: absolutely, that's what pilots are for. we usually run a 2-week pilot: week one is ingest sample traffic and run synthetic replay to calibrate batching/caching; week two runs production-like traces with real sampling to measure tail latency and cost.
[03:05] Sara Gomez: what do costs look like for a 2-week pilot? procurement needs a number to approve.
[03:12] Maya Chen: for Hosted pilot it's usually covered under a credit or low-cost trial for the first X tokens, we can give a firm number in the pricing spreadsheet. Dedicated/Private pilots have more setup overhead — we estimate a one-time onboarding fee plus reserved capacity if you want strict guarantees. i'll include approximate pilot numbers in the spreadsheet.
[03:31] Priya Desai: procurement asked about vendor comparisons — we tried a POC with one of the big cloud providers and the per-token egress and model overhead was higher than advertised when we scaled. how does Redwood avoid that?
[03:44] Maya Chen: two things — our runtime is GPU-optimized and picks kernels per model/sequence length, and we do smart routing + KV/prefix caching to reduce repeat compute. also in Dedicated we can pin capacity and avoid noisy neighbors. but we'll show side-by-side unit-econ estimates in the sheet.
[03:58] Marcus Lee: on caching — how stateful is the cache? we have sessions that last minutes with lots of small updates.
[04:04] Leo Park: our prefix cache (KV) stores key-value states keyed by session or prompt prefix. it's TTL-based, and we support approximate matching and partial reuse. for your use-case with short incremental updates, you can get a lot of reuse if the majority of the prompt is shared. keep in mind, if contexts are highly unique we won't see big wins.
[04:23] Priya Desai: and security — SOC2? audit logs? SAML?
[04:28] Maya Chen: yes SOC2 Type II, SSO via SAML/SCIM, RBAC, detailed audit logs, and you can bring your own KMS for Private/Dedicated. we'll share the SOC2 report and an architecture diagram.
[04:39] Sara Gomez: network egress for Private — we need to confirm VPC peering and egress costs.
[04:44] Leo Park: for Private VPC the traffic stays in your network if on-prem or VPC peering; egress depends on your cloud provider for outbound beyond the region. we'll include typical egress patterns in the docs.
[04:56] Marcus Lee: regarding throughput — you mentioned continuous batching. what batch sizes and latencies should we expect at 200 p95?
[05:03] Leo Park: batching is adaptive — at high QPS we form larger batches to amortize kernel launch overhead. typical batch sizes depend on model and sequence length; for your 220-token prompts and 80-token outputs, we might see average batch sizes of 8–16 at 200 p95, which reduces per-token latency/cost but we tune to keep 95th latency within your SLO.
[05:23] Marcus Lee: are there SLOs on Dedicated? we need an SLA for production.
[05:27] Maya Chen: Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime and latency targets; we'll include the SLA terms in the sales packet. public Hosted SLAs differ by tier but for production-scale we'll recommend Dedicated if you need strict guarantees.
[05:40] Priya Desai: timeline question: if we decide to go pilot in mid-november, what's realistic?
[05:45] Leo Park: hosted pilot can start within days, Dedicated pilot requires a 1–2 week provisioning window plus config for KV cache and autoscaling rules. Private on-prem can take longer — depends on infra approvals.
[05:56] Sara Gomez: procurement will want an estimated monthly run rate at steady state with dedicated capacity assumptions. can you provide both hosted per-token projection and dedicated committed-cost model?
[06:04] Maya Chen: yes, that's part of the spreadsheet — we'll model sample traffic with hit-rate assumptions for caching and quantization tiers. i'll make conservative and optimistic scenarios.
[06:12] Marcus Lee: for the model variants — can you serve quantized A100/4-bit models? what's the quality variance?
[06:18] Leo Park: we support quantized model variants that run faster and use less memory. on ranking/retrieval tasks the quality delta is usually <2% for top-k metrics in many cases but again we'll run your evals.
[06:30] Priya Desai: okay, next steps? we want pricing + pilot plan + security docs.
[06:34] Maya Chen: action items recap: I'll send pricing and unit-econ workbook; Leo will send benchmark plan and a short list of required traffic artifacts; Marcus will share sample traces and prompts; Priya will confirm procurement timeline. we aim to have a decision point after the 2-week pilot with a recommended deployment path.
[06:51] Sara Gomez: sounds good. one more question — do you have references of retailers who did a similar migration from hosted to dedicated?
[06:57] Maya Chen: yes i can share 1–2 anonymized case studies — i'll include those links in the email.
[07:03] Priya Desai: ok thanks everyone. we should sync again after we review the spreadsheet.
[07:07] Maya Chen: great, we'll send materials by friday. thanks all.
